concepts.title: Measurement of Time
concepts.definition: Time is measured by anything that repeats regularly: from the ancients' sundials and water clocks to pendulum clocks and modern quartz watches, a periodic event becomes a clock.
concepts.key_idea: A clock is a steady repeater: the more regular the repeat, the better the timekeeper.
question_patterns: what is periodic motion and how does it measure time
how did people measure time before clocks
how does a pendulum clock work
what makes quartz watches accurate

solution_steps.explain: Say what the concept means in one or two lines.

concepts.title: Slow or Fast: Comparing Motion
concepts.definition: Motion is judged slow or fast by comparing the distance covered in the same time: the runner who covers more metres in one second is faster, which is why races are timed to a blink.
concepts.key_idea: Same time, more distance means faster: comparison needs a common clock.
question_patterns: how do we decide which of two motions is faster
why do we compare distances in the same time
who is faster, one covering 100 m in 12 s or 100 m in 15 s
how are races decided when runners finish together
give two examples of slow and fast motion

solution_steps.explain: Write the two ideas or groups side by side.
Note the points on which they differ and one point they share.
State in one line what the comparison teaches.

concepts.title: Speed and Its Calculation
concepts.definition: Speed is the distance covered in unit time, calculated as total distance divided by total time; its SI unit is metre per second, and kilometres per hour serve longer journeys.
concepts.key_idea: One formula compresses a journey: distance over time gives a number everyone can compare.
question_patterns: define speed and write its formula
what is the si unit of speed
find the speed of a cyclist covering 100 m in 20 s
a car covers 60 km in one hour what is its speed
convert km per hour into metre per second
calculate which of two walkers is faster

solution_steps.explain: Write the distance covered with its unit.
Write the time taken with its unit.
The quotient is the speed in metre per second when units are si.

concepts.title: Uniform and Non-uniform Linear Motion
concepts.definition: Motion along a straight line is uniform when equal distances pass in equal times, as a metro cruising between stations, and non-uniform when the pace changes, as city traffic that speeds, slows and halts.
concepts.key_idea: Equal beats in equal times mark uniform motion: unequal distances in equal times betray non-uniform motion.

solution_steps.explain: Write the two ideas or groups side by side.
Note the points on which they differ and one point they share.
State in one line what the comparison teaches.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Prerna runs the 100 metre sprint in 12.5 seconds. Calculate her speed in m/s.

solution_template.explain: Speed equals total distance divided by total time.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Swati cycles 3.6 km to school in 15 minutes. Find her speed in m/s.

solution_template.explain: 3.6 km is 3600 m and 15 minutes is 900 s.
3600 m in 900 s gives the speed in m/s.

worked_examples.question_pattern: how is the speed of an object calculated?

solution_template.explain: Write out the parts, kinds or steps involved.
Say how one part leads to the next or one kind differs from the other.
Give the overall picture in one sentence.
